title: Etiquette & language
body:
Shoes come off at ryokan entrances, temple interiors, and some restaurants with tatami seating — Kurayoshi's old-town eateries and any Misasa Onsen ryokan both apply. Wash and rinse fully at the shower stalls before getting into a shared bath at Kabuyu or a ryokan's onsen; swimwear isn't worn in the water.

⚠ Tattoo policy varies by venue and this pass could not confirm Kabuyu's or any specific Misasa ryokan's individual policy — Japan's tourism agency has told operators that a blanket tattoo ban isn't appropriate, but many onsen still enforce one. If anyone in the party has visible tattoos, ask directly (or look for a private-bath option) before assuming access.

English signage thins out once you're past Tottori Station — the phrase card in the Trip kit tab is worth using at Kurayoshi/Misasa restaurants and the bus stop.
